# MCP tool reference

<!-- Generated by docs/scripts/gen-mcp-reference.mjs from `scriber mcp --headless`; run `npm run docs:mcp` after changing tools. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every tool Scriber offers AI agents, as the server lists them (74 tools). Units are
millimetres, y grows down, angles are degrees clockwise. Most tools also take an optional
`document` (a document id from `list_documents`); without it they work on the active tab.

## activate_document

Show a document to the person (make it the active tab). Only when they asked to see it: switching tabs changes what they are looking at.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | integer | yes | The document's id (list_documents). |

## add_annotation

Pin a comment on the canvas for the person (at a point, or on items). Not lasered or exported. Returns its id.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text` | string | yes |  |
| `at` | number[] |  | Where the pin goes (mm); default the centre of items. |
| `items` | integer[] |  | Item ids it is about. |
| `author` | string |  | Your name, shown on the comment (default "agent"). |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## add_constraint

Add a geometric constraint (AutoCAD GEOMCONSTRAINT): coincident, collinear, concentric, fix, parallel, perpendicular, horizontal, vertical, tangent, smooth, symmetric or equal; or regular (one {kind: item} ref: a closed straight-sided shape keeps equal sides and corners, as polygons from add_items do). The geometry moves to satisfy it at once and stays bound from then on. Refused (with the conflicting constraints named) if it cannot be satisfied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | [Kind](#type-kind) | yes | A geometric constraint (not dim_*). Two-object constraints keep the first object and move the second, as in AutoCAD. |
| `refs` | [Ref](#type-ref)[] | yes | The geometry: e.g. [{"kind":"segment","item":3,"segment":0}, {"kind":"point","item":4,"vertex":1}]. Symmetric takes the two objects, then the symmetry line. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## add_dimensional_constraint

Add a dimensional constraint (AutoCAD DIMCONSTRAINT): a named parameter (d1, ang1, rad1, dia1) that drives the geometry to its value. The value can be a number or an expression of other parameters. The dimension shows on the drawing as name=value.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `type` | [DimType](#type-dimtype) | yes |  |
| `refs` | [Ref](#type-ref)[] | yes | Two points, or one line (linear, aligned); two lines (angular); an arc or circle segment (radius, diameter). |
| `name` | string |  | Parameter name; default d1, ang1, rad1, dia1, …. |
| `value` | any |  | A number (mm or degrees) or an expression of other parameters such as "d1 / 2". Default: what it measures now. |
| `offset` | number |  | Where the dimension is drawn: mm from the geometry (linear, aligned), the arc radius (angular), or the leader angle in degrees (radius, diameter). Default 8 / 0. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## add_items

Add items (line, rect, circle, arc, polygon, polyline, path, curve (Bézier), text, dimension) and guide lines (xline, ray, centerline, centermark: construction lines for drawing, never lasered or exported), each on a layer (by id, or by op: the first layer with it). Returns ids and the items compactly (id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation, contour/vertex counts; verbose: true for geometry). Big batches: write the items array to a JSON file and pass its path instead of items. One undo step. The old fill: true is still accepted and means op engrave.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | [NewItem](#type-newitem)[] |  |  |
| `path` | string |  | Or a JSON file (absolute path) holding the same items array (or {"items": [...]}), for big batches. |
| `select` | boolean |  | Select the new items in the GUI (default false: the user's selection stays as it is). |
| `infer` | boolean |  | Join the new items to what they touch, as drawing in the GUI does (INFER): coincident on ends and centres within 1e-6 mm of another item's, concentric for shared arc centres. Default false. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## add_layer

Add a layer at the end with a name and op (cut, score, engrave, no_output). A taken name gets a number. Returns the layers.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes |  |
| `op` | [Op](#type-op) | yes |  |
| `current` | boolean |  | Make it the layer new shapes drawn in the GUI go on. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## align

Align (AutoCAD ALIGN, empty ids = the selection): move the items so source1 lands on dest1; with source2/dest2 also rotate them so source1→source2 points along dest1→dest2, and with scale also size them to match.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Items to move; empty = the selection. |
| `source1` | number[] | yes |  |
| `dest1` | number[] | yes |  |
| `source2` | number[] |  | Second pair: the items also turn so source1→source2 lies along dest1→dest2. |
| `dest2` | number[] |  |  |
| `scale` | boolean |  | With a second pair: also scale so the two lines have the same length. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## array_polar

Copy items around a centre (empty ids = the selection): count items in total spread over angle degrees (default 360 = evenly round, positive = clockwise). rotate (default true) turns each copy; false keeps its orientation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  |  |
| `count` | integer | yes | Items in total, the original included. |
| `centre` | number[] | yes |  |
| `angle` | number |  | Degrees to spread them over, positive = clockwise; default 360 (evenly round). |
| `rotate` | boolean |  | Turn the copies with the angle (default true); false only moves them. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## array_rectangular

Copy items into a grid (empty ids = the selection): rows × columns in total, the original being the top-left cell, dx mm between columns and dy between rows.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  |  |
| `rows` | integer | yes |  |
| `columns` | integer | yes |  |
| `dx` | number |  | Distance between columns in mm (negative = to the left). |
| `dy` | number |  | Distance between rows in mm (positive = down). |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## auto_constrain

Infer constraints (AutoCAD AUTOCONSTRAIN) for items (empty = the selection): coincident ends, horizontal, vertical, parallel, perpendicular, tangent, concentric and equal, within the tolerances. Returns the new constraints.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Item ids; empty = the selection. |
| `tolerance` | number |  | Distance tolerance in mm (default 0.05). |
| `angle_tolerance` | number |  | Angle tolerance in degrees (default 1). |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## boolean

Union, difference or intersection of two or more closed paths (empty ids = the selection). Difference subtracts the others from the first id. The result replaces the first item, keeping its name, layer and so its op (the other items' layers do not matter: a no-output cutter subtracted from a cut part leaves a cut part); holes become contours of a compound path; the other items are deleted. Returns the result compactly (verbose: true for its geometry).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Two or more closed paths; empty = the selection. For difference the first one is the base. |
| `operation` | [BoolOp](#type-boolop) | yes |  |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## break_apart

Split a compound path into one item per contour.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer |  | Item id; missing = the single selected item. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## break_item

Break a path (AutoCAD BREAK) at the point nearest `at`: an open path splits in two items, a closed one opens there. With at2 the piece between the two points is removed instead (a closed shape loses the shorter way round). Returns the ids of the pieces.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `at` | number[] | yes | Break point (the nearest point on the path). |
| `at2` | number[] |  | Second point: the piece between `at` and `at2` is removed (on a closed shape the shorter way round). |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## chamfer

Cut corners off with a straight line (empty ids = the selection): the corner nearest `at`, or every sharp corner. distance goes back along the incoming side, distance2 (default = distance) along the outgoing one. Two open lines/polylines are joined where they meet, like fillet. With `first` and `second`, chamfers two picked objects as AutoCAD does (lines, arcs and end segments of open polylines; not circles): distance from the corner along the first (along the arc for arcs), distance2 along the second; 0 and 0 makes a sharp corner. Returns the new and changed ids.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Item ids; empty = the selection. Two open lines/polylines are joined where they meet, and that corner is cut. |
| `distance` | number | yes | How far back along the incoming side (or the first item) the cut starts, in mm. |
| `distance2` | number |  | Along the outgoing side (or the second item); default = distance. |
| `at` | number[] |  | Only cut the corner nearest this point; missing = every sharp corner. |
| `first` | [ObjectPick](#type-objectpick) |  | Two-object form (AutoCAD FILLET/CHAMFER picking two objects): the first object and where it was picked; needs `second` too, and then `ids` and `at` are ignored. |
| `second` | [ObjectPick](#type-objectpick) |  | The second object and where it was picked. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## close_document

Close a document's tab. Refuses when it has unsaved changes unless discard_changes is true (ask the person first). Closing the last tab leaves a new empty document.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | integer | yes | The document's id (list_documents). |
| `discard_changes` | boolean |  | Close it although it has unsaved changes (they are lost). |

## combine_items

Combine paths into one compound path (empty ids = the selection). Holes stay empty when engraved. Keeps the first item's name and op.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Item ids; empty = the user's current selection. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## delete_constraints

Delete constraints by id, and/or every constraint on the given items (AutoCAD DELCONSTRAINT). The geometry stays where it is.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Constraint ids. |
| `items` | integer[] |  | Also every constraint on these items (AutoCAD DELCONSTRAINT). |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## delete_items

Delete items (empty ids = the selection).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Item ids; empty = the user's current selection. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## delete_layer

Delete a layer. Its items move to move_to; without move_to a layer with items is refused. The last layer cannot be deleted.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `move_to` | integer |  | Layer to move the items to; without it a layer that has items is not deleted. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## duplicate_items

Copy items, offset by dx/dy (empty ids = the selection).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  |  |
| `dx` | number |  |  |
| `dy` | number |  |  |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## explode

Explode (AutoCAD EXPLODE, empty ids = the selection): a compound path becomes one item per contour, a single path one item per line or arc segment, a text one path of its letter outlines. Returns the new ids.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Item ids; empty = the user's current selection. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## export_library

Save machines and materials to a Scriber library file (.scrlib) to share with other Scriber users. Both lists missing = the whole library; the machines the materials' settings use are included.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Where to write the library file (.scrlib). |
| `machines` | string[] |  | Machine ids; with both lists missing everything is exported. |
| `materials` | string[] |  | Material ids; the machines their settings use are added. |

## export_png

Render the document to PNG (preview: true shows what the laser makes). With a path it is written to that file; without, the image is returned so you can see the drawing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string |  | Where to write the PNG. Without a path the image is returned so you can look at it. |
| `dpi` | number |  | Resolution; default: 2048 px on the material's longest side. Images returned inline stay under 8000 px. |
| `include_annotations` | boolean |  | Default true. |
| `preview` | boolean |  | Render what the laser makes instead of the drawing: material colour, burned areas, thin cut and score lines, cut-out pieces shadowed with their holes open; no-output items and guides hidden. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## export_svg

Export the document as SVG in mm for laser software (red = cut, blue = score, black = engrave lines and filled areas), one group (Inkscape layer) per shown layer in laser order; hidden layers are left out.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes |  |
| `include_annotations` | boolean |  | Include no_output items (notes, dimensions, helpers). Default false, because laser software would burn them. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## export_xs

Export the document as an xTool Studio project (.xs) for the document's xTool machine and laser module: one colour layer per shown cut/score/engrave layer, each with its processing type (cut, score = vector engraving, engrave = fill) and the layer's power, speed and passes (and lines per cm). Text goes out as outlines; no-output and hidden layers, guides and dimensions are left out; images are skipped (listed in `skipped`).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes | Where to write the .xs project. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## extend

Extend (AutoCAD EXTEND) the open end of a path nearest `at` until it meets the nearest boundary ahead of it (lines along their direction, arcs round their circle). Boundaries default to every other path and guide line.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer | yes |  |
| `at` | number[] | yes | A point near the open end to extend. |
| `boundaries` | integer[] |  | Boundary items; empty = every other path and guide line. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## fillet

Round corners with an arc (empty ids = the selection): the corner nearest `at`, or every sharp corner between straight segments. With exactly two open lines/polylines, they are extended or shortened to meet, joined into one path, and that corner is rounded (AutoCAD FILLET of two objects). With `first` and `second` (each an id and the point it was picked at), fillets any two objects as AutoCAD does: lines, arcs, circles and end segments of open polylines (lines touching end to end count as one polyline); the picks choose the kept sides and which arc is meant, lines and arcs are trimmed or extended to the arc, circles stay, two open paths become one, parallel lines get a half-circle cap, radius 0 makes a sharp corner. Returns the new and changed ids.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Item ids; empty = the selection. Two open lines/polylines are joined where they meet, and that corner is rounded. |
| `radius` | number | yes | Arc radius in mm (0 with two open items just joins them into a sharp corner). |
| `at` | number[] |  | Only round the corner nearest this point; missing = every sharp corner. |
| `first` | [ObjectPick](#type-objectpick) |  | Two-object form (AutoCAD FILLET/CHAMFER picking two objects): the first object and where it was picked; needs `second` too, and then `ids` and `at` are ignored. |
| `second` | [ObjectPick](#type-objectpick) |  | The second object and where it was picked. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## get_document

Get the document: material size, notes, layers, the user's selection, and every item (or only ids) with op, bounding box, rotation and its geometry. geometry: false gives a summary without geometry; a large document gets the summary unless geometry is set, with a note saying so: then ask for the geometry of particular ids.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Only these items; empty = all. Picked items come with their geometry unless geometry is false. |
| `geometry` | boolean |  | true: every item's geometry; false: summary only (id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation, contour and vertex counts). Default: geometry, unless the reply would be very large. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## get_laser_setup

The document's machine, laser module and material, the material library's settings per operation (null where the library has none), and per layer the setting the laser uses: the preset for the layer's op with the layer's own power/speed/passes on top (null when neither gives them).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## group

Group items (empty ids = the selection) so they are picked together; an item leaves any group it was in.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Item ids; empty = the user's current selection. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## import_image

Import an image from a file or base64 data. It is converted to greyscale and placed as an engraved item. Returns the item.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string |  | File to import (PNG, JPEG, WebP, BMP, GIF, TIFF). |
| `data_base64` | string |  | Or the image bytes, base64 encoded. |
| `x` | number |  |  |
| `y` | number |  |  |
| `width` | number |  | Width in mm; height follows the aspect ratio. Default 10 px per mm, capped to the material. |
| `name` | string |  |  |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## import_library

Merge a Scriber library file (.scrlib) into the user's library. on_conflict (replace / keep_both / skip) decides for ids taken by a different machine or material; keep_both gives the import a new id. Reports added, replaced, skipped and machines the settings need that the user does not have.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | yes |  |
| `on_conflict` | [OnConflict](#type-onconflict) | yes | For a machine or material whose id is taken by a different one. |

## import_svg

Import an SVG file (path) or SVG text/base64 (data). Each path becomes an item (subpaths stay one compound path), curves become arcs, text becomes outlines and raster images greyscale images. Stroke colour sets the op: red = cut, blue = score, black/dark = engrave, grey or green = no_output, other colours = cut. A fill on a closed path means engrave the area, except a grey or green fill (no_output); a path with both a fill and a stroke becomes two items (the fill's op, then the stroke's) unless both give the same op. A path with neither fill nor stroke (or a fully transparent fill) comes in as no_output, handy as a boolean cutter. Each item goes on the current layer when that has its op, else on the first layer with it. Units in the file (mm, cm, in) are honoured; plain numbers are px at 96 per inch. Returns ids and items (compact, verbose: true for geometry), each with svg_id (the element's id, empty when it has none) and element (index of the SVG path/image in document order; one element can give two items).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string |  | SVG file to import. |
| `data` | string |  | Or the SVG itself: its text, or base64. |
| `x` | number |  | Left edge of the drawing in mm; default: where the file puts it. |
| `y` | number |  | Top edge of the drawing in mm; default: where the file puts it. |
| `width` | number |  | Scale the drawing to this width in mm (overrides scale). |
| `scale` | number |  | Extra factor on the file's own size; 1.333 (96/72) for 72 DPI files. Default 1. |
| `tolerance` | number |  | Largest distance in mm between a curve and the arcs that replace it. Default 0.01. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## list_documents

List the open documents (the tabs in Scriber's window): document id, name, path, unsaved, active (the one the person sees) and item count. Every document tool takes document: &lt;id>; without it, it works on the active tab.

## list_fonts

List the font families installed on this computer, for a text's font. sans-serif, serif and monospace also work and pick the system's default of that kind.

## list_layers

List the layers in order: id, name, op, colour, own settings (power/speed/passes that override the material library), visible, locked, number of items, whether it is current, and laser_setting: the power/speed/passes the laser uses (library preset for the op with the layer's own numbers on top; null when neither gives them).

## list_materials

List the material library: each material with its thickness, color (preview sheet colour [r, g, b], missing = wood) and laser settings per machine, laser module and operation (cut, score, engrave): power %, speed mm/s, passes, and for engrave line_interval (mm between lines; tell people lines per cm = 10 / line_interval) and bidirectional.

## stretch

Stretch (AutoCAD STRETCH): every point of the items that lies inside the crossing window moves by dx/dy, the others stay, so the lines between them stretch. Whole circles, texts and images move when their centre/anchor is inside. One undo step. Returns the changed ids.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` | number[] | yes | Crossing window [x, y, width, height]: every point inside it moves. |
| `dx` | number | yes |  |
| `dy` | number | yes |  |
| `ids` | integer[] |  | Only these items; empty = every item the window catches. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## transform_items

Move, rotate, scale and/or mirror items (empty ids = the selection). Order: mirror, scale, rotate around the pivot, then move by dx/dy. The pivot defaults to the centre of the items' bounding box. Each item's rotation (see get_document) adds the rotate angle; a mirror negates it; a non-uniform scale resets it to 0 unless the item's angle is a multiple of 90°. copy: true transforms copies and keeps the originals (a mirrored copy: mirror_x or mirror_y with copy).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ids` | integer[] |  |  |
| `dx` | number |  |  |
| `dy` | number |  |  |
| `rotate` | number |  | Degrees, positive = clockwise on screen. |
| `scale_x` | number |  | Scale factors; 0 or missing means 1. |
| `scale_y` | number |  |  |
| `mirror_x` | boolean |  | Mirror left-right / top-bottom. |
| `mirror_y` | boolean |  |  |
| `pivot` | number[] |  | Centre of rotation/scale/mirror; defaults to the centre of the items' bounding box. |
| `copy` | boolean |  | Transform copies and leave the originals where they are (e.g. mirror_x with copy for a mirrored copy). |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

## trim

Trim a path (AutoCAD TRIM): the piece around `at` is removed back to the nearest crossings with the cutting edges (default: every other path). An open line keeps the parts on either side; a closed shape needs two crossings and becomes open. An item with nothing left is deleted. Constraints on the item follow what is left (a trimmed circle's tangents move to the arc), and each new end stays on its cutting edge unless constrain is false.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | integer |  | The item to trim; missing = the single selected item. |
| `at` | number[] | yes | A point on the piece to remove. |
| `edges` | integer[] |  | Cutting edges; empty = every other path. |
| `constrain` | boolean |  | Keep each new end on the edge it was trimmed against (a coincident constraint, as INFER does while drawing). Default true. |
| `verbose` | boolean |  | Reply with each item's full geometry. Default false: id, name, layer, op, kind, bbox, rotation and (paths) contour and vertex counts; get_document with ids gives the geometry later. |
| `document` | integer |  | The open document to work on (id from list_documents); missing = the active tab, the one the person sees. |

Change a layer: name, op (changes what the laser does with all its items), color, settings (the layer's own power/speed/passes; missing = material library), visible, locked, order (position) and current. One undo step.

| `settings` | [Overrides](#type-overrides) |  | Replaces the layer's own power (%), speed (mm/s) and passes; a missing one (or {}) uses the material library's preset for the layer's op. |

## wait_for_annotations

Wait until the person adds, replies to, resolves or reopens a comment after since_revision (missing = now), or timeout_s passes (default 60, max 300). Returns at once when there already is one. Watches every open document unless document is given; each annotation in the reply says its document (id), so pass that to reply_annotation. Reply: annotations (the changed ones, as list_annotations) and revision; pass that revision to the next call. timed_out: true when nothing came. Loop on it to follow the person's review.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | integer |  | Only this open document's comments; missing = every open document (each reply names its document). |
| `since_revision` | integer |  | The revision from the last list_annotations / wait_for_annotations reply; missing = now. |
| `timeout_s` | number |  | Seconds to wait (default 60, at most 300). |

## Types

The argument types the tools above refer to.

### BoolOp {#type-boolop}

One of: `union` \| `difference` \| `intersection`
- `union`: Everything covered by any of the shapes.
- `difference`: The first shape minus all the others.
- `intersection`: Only what all the shapes cover.

### Category {#type-category}

What kind of material it is, so a long list can be filtered.

One of: `paper` \| `wood` \| `plywood` \| `acrylic` \| `leather` \| `fabric` \| `metal` \| `stone` \| `glass` \| `other`

### Contour {#type-contour}

One closed or open outline.


| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `vertices` | [Vertex](#type-vertex)[] | yes |  |
| `closed` | boolean |  |  |

### CurveSegment {#type-curvesegment}

One segment of a curve.


| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `to` | number[] | yes |  |
| `controls` | number[][] |  | 0 = straight line, 1 = quadratic, 2 = cubic Bézier control points. |

### DimType {#type-dimtype}

One of: `horizontal` \| `vertical` \| `radius` \| `diameter` \| `linear` \| `aligned` \| `angular`
- `linear`: Horizontal or vertical, whichever the points are further apart in.
- `aligned`: Straight distance (two points, a line's length, or a point to a line).
- `angular`: Between two lines, in degrees.

### Kind {#type-kind}

What a constraint keeps true. The geometric kinds are AutoCAD's GEOMCONSTRAINT, the `dim_*`
kinds its DIMCONSTRAINT.

One of: `parallel` \| `perpendicular` \| `dim_radial` \| `dim_diameter` \| `coincident` \| `collinear` \| `concentric` \| `fix` \| `horizontal` \| `vertical` \| `tangent` \| `smooth` \| `symmetric` \| `equal` \| `regular` \| `dim_horizontal` \| `dim_vertical` \| `dim_aligned` \| `dim_angular`
- `coincident`: Two points on top of each other, or a point on a line (its extension) or a circle/arc.
- `collinear`: Two lines on one infinite line.
- `concentric`: Two arcs/circles with the same centre.
- `fix`: A point, segment, centre or whole item stays where it is.
- `horizontal`: A line, or two points, level.
- `vertical`: A line, or two points, plumb.
- `tangent`: A line and an arc/circle, or two arcs/circles, touching without crossing.
- `smooth`: Two segments joined end to end with no kink (G1); two arcs also get the same radius (G2).
- `symmetric`: Two points, lines or arcs/circles mirrored over a symmetry line (the third reference).
- `equal`: Two lines the same length, or two arcs/circles the same radius.
- `regular`: A closed straight-sided item (one contour) stays a regular polygon: equal sides, equal corners.
- `dim_horizontal`: Horizontal distance between two points (or a line's ends).
- `dim_vertical`: Vertical distance between two points (or a line's ends).
- `dim_aligned`: Straight distance between two points, a line's length, or a point's distance to a line.
- `dim_angular`: Angle between two lines, in degrees.

### OnConflict {#type-onconflict}

What to do when an imported machine or material has the id of a different one already in the library.

One of: `replace` \| `skip` \| `keep_both`
- `keep_both`: Import it under a new id.

### Op {#type-op}

What the laser does with an item (the four operations of xTool Studio).

One of: `cut` \| `score` \| `engrave` \| `no_output`
- `cut`: Cut through the material along the line (red in SVG).
- `score`: Mark a line without cutting through (blue in SVG).
- `engrave`: Burn the area inside closed shapes, text and images (holes stay empty; black in SVG). Open shapes have no area: they are scored (see `Item::effective_op`).
- `no_output`: Notes, guides and dimensions for people; never sent to the laser (grey). Old files and clients may say "annotate" or "none".

### Operation {#type-operation}

What the laser does, as far as settings go (the item ops that reach the laser).

One of: `cut` \| `score` \| `engrave`
- `cut`: Cut through.
- `score`: Mark a thin line.
- `engrave`: Engrave a whole area, line by line. Older libraries had separate "engrave" (line) and "fill" keys.

### Overrides {#type-overrides}

A layer's own laser numbers; a missing one comes from the material library's preset for the op.

|---|---|---|---|
| `power` | number |  | Power in percent (0–100). |
| `speed` | number |  | Speed in mm/s. |
| `passes` | integer |  |  |
